Acceptance criteria describe concrete externally observable outcomes rather than intent: named diagnostics (e.g. AC-014 'gate-id-duplicate', AC-039 'capability-id-duplicate', AC-024 'unknown-fragment-id'/'fragment-selector-required'), specific fixture shapes and expected pass/fail results (AC-004's dedicated negative fixtures for a missing delivery_strategy key and a delivery_strategy object missing kind), and byte-level/exit-code assertions (AC-026's --check exit codes, AC-031's byte-identical wrapper output). No AC in this package is a vague statement of intent.

Non-goals is explicit and itemized: excludes implementing Epic A1's schema/canonicalizer, Epic A5's Resolver, any Capability Pack content, freezing the lite-upgrade-reason catalog or delivery_strategy.kind vocabulary, Artifact/Promotion Gate behavior, a new plugin, any actual code/contract/test file in this commit (AC-034), and authoring tasks.md/traceability.md or touching AGENTS.md/workflow-state-registry.json in this commit. Each boundary is tied to a concrete blocking mechanism (e.g. check-workflow-state.sh's hard-enforcement) rather than left implicit.

Material constraints are stated where implied: data/versioning (schema=='capability-registry/v1', per-artifact version checks in REQ-005), security/provider-neutrality (REQ-003(g) Provider-name contamination scan, ADR-0018 boundary), migration/compatibility (REQ-005's script-relative discovery contract with git-root fallback and fail-closed diagnostics for standalone-installed contexts), and approval boundaries (Roles and Permissions section: Spec-Review-Status stays Pending, human maintainer required to approve and to run protected-file cp steps, agent explicitly barred from writing 'Approved').
